phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: For a coherent spin state, either transverse component normal to the mean spin has variance S/2; the paper defines a squeezed spin state by a transverse variance below S/2. The construction from 2S independent spin-1/2 constituents and the S=1/2 no-squeezing boundary are directly checkable from finite-spin states.
Schematic only: a coherent S-spin state represented by 2S uncorrelated spin-1/2 constituents and a circular uncertainty cone.
Schematic only: a squeezed S-spin state represented by correlated spin-1/2 constituents and an elliptical uncertainty cone.

Exact one-axis-twisting predictions for the mean spin and the unrotated/rotated component variances as functions of S and twist angle mu, including A, B, delta and the extremal variances V_plus and V_minus. These formulas can be checked by direct finite-dimensional evolution under U=exp(-i mu S_z^2/2).
Normalized spherical quasiprobability distribution Q(theta,phi) for the initial coherent state |theta=pi/2,phi=0> at S=20, with reported Q_max=1.
S=20 one-axis-twisted QPD under U=exp(-i mu S_z^2/2) at the reported optimum mu=0.199, normalized by its reported maximum Q_max=0.445; the narrow axis is rotated by delta.
S=20 one-axis-twisted QPD at mu=0.399, normalized by the reported Q_max=0.241, with the claimed non-geodesic swirliness after excessive twisting.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Section III.A, Eq. (5) and following paragraph, p. 5140
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Large-S, small-|mu| approximation with alpha=S mu/2 and beta=S mu^2/4, leading to the optimal twist magnitude mu_0=24^(1/6) S^(-2/3) and minimum variance V_min approximately (1/2)(S/3)^(1/3). The stated small-S deviation and large-S approach are numerically testable.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Section III.A, paragraph after Eq. (5), p. 5140
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: The normalized uncertainty product U_yz=4 Var(S_y) Var(S_z)/|<S_x>|^2 is claimed to obey approximately 1+(mu/mu_0)^6 and remain near the minimum-uncertainty value for |mu|<mu_0.
Two-axis countertwisting is defined by H=hbar chi(S_{pi/2,pi/4}^2-S_{pi/2,-pi/4}^2)=hbar chi(S_+^2-S_-^2)/(2i); its equivalence and finite-spin dynamics are independently computable.
Normalized spherical QPD for the S=20 initial coherent state |theta=0,phi>, with reported Q_max=1.
S=20 two-axis-countertwisted QPD under the Eq. (6) unitary at reported optimum mu=0.203, normalized by the reported Q_max=0.252, with contraction and stretching along orthogonal geodesics.
S=20 two-axis-countertwisted QPD at mu=0.248, normalized by the reported Q_max=0.187, with the distribution claimed to split into two parts.

Single-panel quantitative plot of exact minimum attainable transverse variance versus S for one-axis and two-axis squeezing, together with the CSS line S/2 and broken asymptotes (1/2)(S/3)^(1/3) and 1/2. The caption states that the omitted S=1 special case reaches zero.

Beyond Figure 4, the paper claims that the two-axis minimum is below 1/2 at small S and tends to 1/2 as S grows, while the enhanced variance reaches S^2/2 and the mean spin remains of order S; at S=1 either twisting mechanism can drive one component variance exactly to zero.
Schwinger-spin mapping for N particles in two interferometer arms: S_+=sum_k a_k^dagger b_k=S_x+iS_y and S_z=(N_A-N_B)/2, with total spin S=N/2 under mode-coherent linear optics.
Schematic only: one particle in two interferometer arms represented as an abstract spin-1/2.

For equally partitioned quanta, the paper relates number-difference noise to 2 sqrt(Var(S_z)) and phase noise to sqrt(Var(S_y))/|<S_x>|, obtains delta_N delta_phi >=1, and gives the coherent 50-percent beamsplitter benchmarks delta_N=sqrt(N) and delta_phi approximately 1/sqrt(N).

N two-level atoms are mapped to total spin S=N/2, with S_z equal to half the population difference and S_x,S_y the dipole quadratures; the one-axis term is quadratic in population difference and the two-axis term is simultaneous two-atom excitation/de-excitation.

Closed-form coherent-state matrix-element identities for <S_+ exp[i mu(S_z+1/2)]>, its squared counterpart, and its derivative-weighted counterpart. These are independently checkable by direct matrix algebra and underpin the exact one-axis moments.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The paper-exact coherent-state formula, frozen grid, isolated run, unit peak, state norm, Q bound, and Husimi resolution-of-identity all agree with an independent construction.

independent_checks.claim: The S=20 coherent-state Husimi distribution has unit peak and satisfies the normalized spherical resolution of identity.
A clean-room binomial coherent-state construction regenerates every frozen T001 grid value exactly.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: A normalization or coherent-state-orientation error could reproduce the apparent Figure 2(a) panel while violating the paper's unit-peak claim.
falsification_attempts.method: Construct the binomial coherent-state overlap independently, maximize it, and integrate it over the full sphere with Gauss-Legendre quadrature.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The paper's one-axis unitary and parameters are used exactly; a clean-room direct-phase implementation reproduces the frozen array, and a full printed-mu rounding sweep contains a Q maximum that rounds to the caption value 0.445.

independent_checks.claim: Direct application of exp(-i mu m^2/2) to independently constructed spin-20 amplitudes regenerates the frozen T002 Q grid exactly.
Sweeping mu over its three-decimal rounding interval gives Qmax in [0.4453807073, 0.4471910688], consistent with a printed value of 0.445.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The reproduced agreement is an artifact of a factor-of-two error in the one-axis unitary rather than the paper's convention.
falsification_attempts.method: Replace exp(-i mu S_z^2/2) by exp(-i mu S_z^2), recompute the state, and maximize Q globally before comparing both conventions with the caption and rounding sweep.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The paper-exact overtwisted one-axis state is reproduced exactly by an independent direct-phase calculation, and the full printed-mu interval gives Qmax values that round to the caption value 0.241.

independent_checks.claim: An independent direct-phase evolution at S=20 and mu=0.399 regenerates the frozen T003 Q grid exactly.
Sweeping mu over [0.3985, 0.3995] gives Qmax in [0.2402966823, 0.2408657217], overlapping values that round to 0.241.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The apparent Figure 2(c) agreement could come from using the doubled one-axis phase convention.
falsification_attempts.method: Double the OAT phase, recompute the full Husimi distribution and global maximum, and compare with the caption and the paper-exact rounding sweep.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The north-pole coherent state follows from the paper's expansion, the mu=0 two-axis unitary is the identity, the independent grid matches exactly, and both unit peak and Husimi normalization pass.

independent_checks.claim: The north-pole coherent state has Qmax=1 and its Husimi distribution integrates to one with the spin-20 resolution factor.
An independent north-pole coherent-state construction regenerates the frozen T004 grid exactly.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: A pole convention or normalization error could invalidate the Figure 3(a) unit-peak claim.
falsification_attempts.method: Evaluate the pole-state overlap directly and integrate Q over the full sphere with Gauss-Legendre quadrature.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: With the paper-exact S=20, mu=0.203 and the correct mu/4 countertwisting generator, spectral evolution, independent dense expm, and high-accuracy DOP853 agree. They give Qmax=0.254470764182679 and a first variance minimum at mu=0.2046374367; both remain outside the caption's three-decimal rounding intervals.

independent_checks.claim: A direct dense matrix exponential gives Qmax=0.2544707641826793 and agrees with the frozen T005 Q grid to 5.72e-15.
High-accuracy DOP853 evolution agrees with dense expm within 3.4e-14 in state amplitude and returns the same Q maximum.
The independently evolved state is normalized and its spin-20 Husimi distribution integrates to 1.0000000000000167.
Across mu in [0.2025, 0.2035], Qmax stays in [0.2532143948, 0.2557329046], and independent covariance minimization gives mu_opt=0.2046374367.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The Figure 3(b) caption values mu=0.203 and Qmax=0.252 are jointly correct within their printed three-decimal precision.
falsification_attempts.method: Sweep the entire mu rounding interval [0.2025, 0.2035], maximize Q globally at each point, compare against [0.2515, 0.2525], and independently minimize the transverse covariance eigenvalue.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: A factor-of-two countertwisting convention can reconcile the independent calculation with the printed Qmax.
falsification_attempts.method: Double the exponent while retaining S=20 and mu=0.203, then repeat the full-sphere maximum search.

discrepancy.paper_claim: Figure 3(b) states S=20, optimally squeezed at mu=0.203 with Q_max=0.252.
discrepancy.independent_result: At mu=0.203, Q_max=0.254470764182679; the exact first variance minimum is at mu=0.2046374367.
discrepancy.observed_gap: Q_max differs by +0.002470764182679 (about +0.98 percent), and mu_opt differs by +0.0016374367.
discrepancy.uncertainty_or_tolerance_basis: Both printed values have three digits after the decimal. Half-unit-last-place intervals for mu and Q_max are disjoint from the independently swept result intervals; numerical-method disagreement is below 7.1e-14 in state amplitude and 5.8e-15 in frozen Q data.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: At the paper-exact S=20 and mu=0.248, spectral evolution, independent dense expm, and DOP853 agree and a converged split-lobe search gives Qmax=0.185588850758101. The full printed-mu rounding interval remains disjoint from the caption's Qmax interval around 0.187.

independent_checks.claim: A direct dense matrix exponential followed by full-sphere split-lobe refinement gives Qmax=0.1855888507581026 and agrees with the frozen T006 grid to 5.01e-15.
High-accuracy DOP853 evolution agrees with dense expm within 7.1e-14 and returns Qmax=0.1855888507581005.
The independently evolved split state is normalized and its Husimi distribution integrates to 1.0000000000000124.
Across mu in [0.2475, 0.2485], Qmax stays in [0.1854555164, 0.1857320898], while grid-to-continuous refinement changes the maximum by only 1.31e-7.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The Figure 3(c) caption value Qmax=0.187 is correct within its printed precision for some mu that rounds to 0.248.
falsification_attempts.method: Sweep mu over [0.2475, 0.2485], maximize Q on a 181x361 sphere, continuously refine every high-value split-lobe candidate, and compare against [0.1865, 0.1875].

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: A factor-of-two countertwisting convention can reconcile the independent split-state calculation with the printed Qmax.
falsification_attempts.method: Double the exponent at S=20 and mu=0.248 and repeat the global split-lobe maximum search.

discrepancy.paper_claim: Figure 3(c) states S=20, mu=0.248 and Q_max=0.187 for the split distribution.
discrepancy.independent_result: At mu=0.248, continuous Q_max=0.185588850758101 with a converged split-lobe search.
discrepancy.uncertainty_or_tolerance_basis: Half-unit-last-place intervals for both printed mu and Q_max remain disjoint after a full mu sweep; grid-to-continuous error is 1.31e-7 and independent state-evolution disagreement is below 7.1e-14.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct covariance minimization with diagonal OAT evolution and sparse expm_multiply TACT evolution reproduces the frozen Figure 4 series to 1.53e-12, confirms the ordering and asymptotic trends, and independently recovers the caption's omitted S=1 zero-variance special case.

independent_checks.claim: Independent diagonal OAT and sparse-exponential TACT evolutions reproduce the frozen minimum-variance values at checked spins with maximum difference 1.53e-12.
At S=1, both twisting mechanisms attain exactly zero transverse variance when the search interval includes the paper-stated special point.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The Figure 4 agreement is a search-bound or wrong-minimum artifact, and the omitted S=1 zero cannot be recovered independently.
falsification_attempts.method: Sample an independent interval, locate the first interior minimum for all plotted spins, and expand the S=1 search beyond the submitted 1.5 bound through mu=pi.

findings.title: Authored scope omits independently inventoried numerical claims
findings.claim: The paper-only inventory contains 17 reproducible numeric items, but the authored scope declares only the seven numerical figure panels. Ten quantitative claim rows are absent; four have no substantive target evidence, so protocol-v2 lifecycle coverage is incomplete.
reproduction_steps: Read Sections II-IV and the Appendix in paper/raw/paper.pdf and enumerate every numerical figure/subfigure plus each independently testable quantitative statement.
List item_id values in contracts/numerical_scope_claims.json and compare source_ref coverage in both directions.
Observe that only Figures 2(a-c), 3(a-c), and 4 have target rows; the ten listed quantitative claim rows are absent, with four having no substantive target evidence.
findings.blocking_reason: A missing numerical item is an explicit protocol-v2 blocking condition even when the seven authored figure targets themselves run successfully.

findings.title: Figure 3(b) printed optimum and Q_max do not survive exact finite-spin checks
findings.claim: Three mutually agreeing paper-exact evolutions yield Q_max=0.254470764182679 at mu=0.203 and the first variance minimum at mu=0.2046374367, rather than the caption's Q_max=0.252 and optimum mu=0.203; the discrepancy survives full printed-value rounding sweeps.
reproduction_steps: Construct S_x and S_y from exact spin-20 ladder coefficients and K=S_x S_y+S_y S_x.
Evolve |S,S> with exp(-i*0.203*K/4), then maximize |<theta,phi|psi>|^2 globally; repeat with DOP853 integration of dpsi/dmu=-i K psi/4.
Sweep mu from 0.2025 through 0.2035 and compare the Q_max interval with [0.2515,0.2525]; independently minimize the transverse covariance eigenvalue.

findings.title: Figure 3(c) printed Q_max is inconsistent with the paper-exact split state
findings.claim: Paper-exact spectral, dense-expm and DOP853 evolutions all give continuous Q_max=0.185588850758101 at mu=0.248, rather than 0.187, and the converged split-lobe discrepancy persists over the full printed-mu rounding interval.
reproduction_steps: Construct the exact spin-20 K generator and evolve |S,S> to mu=0.248 by dense expm and separately by DOP853.
Evaluate Q on a 181x361 sphere and refine every high-value candidate continuously; verify both split lobes and unit normalization.
Sweep mu from 0.2475 through 0.2485 and compare against the printed Q_max interval.

findings.title: Scientific solver bounds and acceptance tolerances have inaccurate or circular provenance
findings.claim: parameter_provenance.json attributes the numerical value 1.5 for both mu search bounds to paper Eqs. (1)-(6), which do not specify that bound; it attributes acceptance tolerances to tests that merely repeat the configured thresholds, and the exact variance_spins marker list is not printed by Figure 4. The frozen inputs are auditable, but these provenance claims are inaccurate or circular.
reproduction_steps: Read solver.one_axis_mu_max, solver.two_axis_mu_max and acceptance in implementation/config/paper_exact.json.
Trace those names through implementation/parameter_provenance.json to the claimed paper-equation and independent-convergence sources.
Inspect paper/raw/paper.pdf Eqs. (1)-(6): no value 1.5 is specified. Inspect implementation/tests/test_model.py: the 0.006 landmark threshold is asserted, not derived.
Confirm in implementation/scripts/run_reproduction.py that these values determine the minimization range and pass/fail gates.
